{{Quote|And that is Fenn Shysa's memorial. Your mother knew him, and your uncle Luke, too. Pay your respects and we can get on with your lessons.|Goran Beviin to Jaina Solo|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
A '''memorial to Fenn Shysa''' was erected by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Bralsin]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Built in honor of the [[Death/Legends|deceased]] [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], [[Fenn Shysa]], it existed as one of only a few memorials ever erected on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world. During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], Fett came to the memorial often to speak with Shysa, something he had only previously done with his deceased [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Hey, do you want to record a holoimage for your mother?''"<br />"''Some cultures would find that disrespectful.''"<br />"''Ah, we don't. Shysa would have ''loved'' it, if it was for Princess Leia. You could even have been a ''Mando'' if your mama had said the word—and if she hadn't met the space bum, of course.|Goran Beviin and Jaina Solo|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
[[Fenn Shysa]]'s memorial was a simple one, consisting of the former [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor's'']] [[Armor/Legends|helmet]] resting atop a column of [[Granite/Legends|granite]] and secured by a [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] peg. Shysa had been a beloved leader to his people, and no [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] would think to steal or dislodge his helmet; the durasteel peg was placed there only as a precaution to thwart bad weather and Mandalore's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Species/Legends|wildlife]]. Located in the small [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]] suburb of [[Bralsin]], the memorial sat at the crest of a small hill, in a clearing surrounded by an avenue of [[Tree/Legends|trees]]. It was a small substitute for a proper ''Mand'alor''{{'s}} grave, but [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] personally considered it fitting for a humble, populist leader like Shysa, to be commemorated like any other Mandalorian. There was no name, inscription, or markings on the monument, and no railings or other indicator that it was a respected leader who was being honored at the site. The memorial itself went undisturbed for at least twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]], surviving the [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attack]] of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], though by [[41 ABY]], the helmet had begun to succumb to rust and the paint had started to noticeably fade.<ref name="Revelation" />

==History==
{{Quote|Shysa led us to kick out the Empire. Didn't you, ''Fen'ika''? A great ''Mand'alor''. But he always wanted Fett as the front man, and Fett wasn't having it. Shysa got his way in the end, though.|Goran Beviin|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
[[File:FennShysa.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Fenn Shysa, the man whom the memorial commemorated]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] Fenn Shysa and two-hundred and eleven other [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] [[Battle of Kamino/Legends|attacked]] the [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] facilities on the [[Water/Legends|watery]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] on behalf of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], devastating them. Though the majority of the Protectors were later [[Death/Legends|killed]] in the fateful [[Mission to Norval II|Battle]] of [[Norval II]], Shysa survived and his deeds did not go unforgotten. Several years later, when the infamous [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] Boba Fett went to Kamino to have his [[cancer]]ous [[Limb/Legends|leg]] transplanted for a new, cloned one, the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Taun We/Legends|Taun We]] hired Fett to kill Shysa in revenge for what he and his comrades had done to Kamino. Fett hunted Shysa—who had by that point become the ''Mand'alor'', leader of the Mandalorian clans—eventually confronting him on the planet [[Shogun (planet)|Shogun]].<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> There, they were attacked by the [[Sevvets]]<ref name="Revelation" /> and Shysa gave his life to protect Fett.<ref name="HotM" /> Shysa had wanted Fett to be ''Mand'alor'' for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]],<ref name="Revelation" /> desiring to capitalize on his [[Clone template/Legends|father]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett's]] reputation as a [[Jedi hunter/Legends|killer of Jedi]] as symbol of strength for [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> and begged Fett to assume the role as his dying wish. Honoring Shysa's last request, Fett became the new ''Mand'alor'', and though he left Shysa's body behind in the [[Quence sector/Legends|Quence sector]], he returned to Mandalore with Shysa's green and red-[[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Armor/Legends|helmet]]. There, in the small [[City/Legends|settlement]] of Bralsin, a rural suburb of the planet's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city, Keldabe, Fett created a simple memorial displaying Shysa's helmet on a column of granite secured by a durasteel peg.<ref name="Revelation" />

The memorial survived the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire|Yuuzhan Vong's]] attack on Mandalore during their invasion of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] unharmed, remaining undisturbed for close to twenty years. During the [[Second Galactic Civil War|conflict]] between the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] and the [[Confederation]], Boba Fett visited Shysa's memorial on a number of occasions, a stark contrast to the nearly twenty years previous when Fett had never bothered to visit the simple monument. There, he would stand and speak to the rusting helmet and imagine Shysa's replies, something he had only previously done with his [[Parent/Legends|father]], Jango. Fett's long-time friend [[Goran Beviin]] later brought [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] to Shysa's memorial during at least one of their training sessions together. While there, Beviin told Solo of Shysa's connection to her mother, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], and her uncle, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], with whom Shysa had fought alongside against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and its later [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|remnants]]. The two paid their respects to the beloved ''Mand'alor''—Beviin even fondly rubbing Shysa's old helmet, and offering to [[Holorecorder/Legends|record]] a [[Hologram/Legends|holoimage]] for Solo's mother, the former [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Leia—then carried on with their lessons.<ref name="Revelation" />

==Behind the scenes==
Fenn Shysa's memorial first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[2008]] novel, ''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'', by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]]. It was later referenced in ''Revelation''{{'s}} ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' sequel, ''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]'', by author [[Troy Denning]], and mentioned in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''{{'s}} entry for "Bralsin."
